claims.statement: EHDS includes health data generated by medical devices and wellness applications among categories relevant to governed secondary use.
EU medical-device rules govern clinical investigations and software or devices with medical intended purposes, making intended use and study design material dependencies.

EHDS secondary-use access is permit-based, may carry proportionate fees, occurs in a secure processing environment and can be refused where serious intellectual-property or trade-secret risk cannot be satisfactorily addressed.

EHDS Chapter IV generally starts applying in March 2029, while its mandatory availability rules for clinical-study and research-cohort data apply from March 2031, so it is not a near-term clinic-data shortcut.
In Poland, device clinical investigations under MDR Articles 62 or 82 require a positive bioethics opinion and URPL authorisation; the exact route depends on the device and protocol.
Established providers already sell end-to-end wearable CRO services, device platforms, analytical and clinical validation, regulatory support, signal quality control and participant operations.

The proposed 2-4 founder-hours per day is plausible only if a qualified principal investigator, clinic coordinator and privacy or quality owner accept the participant-facing and regulated work; those commitments are not yet evidenced.

contrary_evidence: EHDS imposes governance and purpose limits; it does not make clinic data freely licensable or remove MDR clinical-investigation requirements.
EHDS mandatory secondary-use access for clinical studies and research cohorts is phased to 2031, outside the near-term validation period.
VivoSense, Empatica, TNO and Delve already cover large parts of the proposed protocol, device, analytics, regulatory and participant-support stack.
Polish device studies can require both bioethics approval and URPL authorisation, and medical-experiment governance depends on qualified clinical leadership.

economics.acquisition_route: Form one narrow EEG or sleep consortium before building operations: seek at least two noncompeting device sponsors around the same endpoint and a named clinic or principal-investigator team around a costed protocol. This is an unvalidated distribution design; there is no signed sponsor, clinic channel, lead pipeline or measured sales cycle.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: The prior scenario of reaching 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 8-11 remains unvalidated and is not improved by assertion. The redesign creates evidence gates—one paid consortium cohort, repeat sponsor demand, then lawful recurring benchmark revenue—but no sponsor economics, renewal, valuation or wealth timing has been demonstrated.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: the founder limits work to protocol analytics, productization and bounded sponsor coordination within 2-4 hours per day only after a principal investigator, clinic coordinator and privacy or quality owner sign responsibility allocations; the study does not launch otherwise. Availability and terms are unknown.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: sponsor precommitment can cover fixed external cohort costs before launch and leave margin in standardized analysis and later permitted benchmark access. Actual clinic, recruitment, insurance, secure-compute, regulatory and biostatistics quotes are absent, so margin is unknown and the prior 40%-70% range is not treated as evidence.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: a no-launch-until-funded gate reduces founder working-capital exposure compared with paying for a speculative cohort, but founder diligence and sales time remain at risk. Cash timing and payback cannot be estimated until deposits, clinic terms and cohort costs are evidenced.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: founding sponsors split the costed first-cohort clinic, regulatory and study-operation budget through deposits at protocol lock and later milestone payments; recurring benchmark access is offered only after utility and lawful reuse are demonstrated. No sponsor acceptance, price or conversion evidence exists.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: founding sponsors renew for device versions or endpoint updates and later sponsors buy access to permitted reference metrics. No renewal, repeat-purchase or benchmark-licence evidence exists.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Only cohorts with documented reuse rights add comparable derived metrics, protocol failure modes and cross-device reference ranges to the shared benchmark
fingerprint.customer: European EEG and sleep wearable or biosensor teams that share one validation endpoint and could participate as noncompeting founding sponsors
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: A bounded consortium-formation sale to noncompeting EEG or sleep device teams, paired with a named clinic network as proposed delivery partner; operations begin only after sponsor and clinic commitments are documented
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A fixed-scope, single-endpoint sponsor consortium delivering sponsor-specific validation reports and access only to contractually permitted pooled derived benchmarks
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: At least two founding sponsors must pay protocol-lock deposits that cover contracted first-cohort external costs, followed by defined study milestones; no cohort starts before the funding gate is met
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new device or algorithm version needs credible comparison against a stable protocol and clinician labels

founder_fit: Uses the founder's EEG, neuroscience and data-science background on one standardized endpoint rather than a broad CRO stack.
Makes qualified clinic and quality roles a signed pre-launch gate instead of assuming the founder can cover participant-facing or regulated work.
Makes sponsor funding a pre-launch gate, seeking to avoid committing the founder's free capital to an unfunded cohort while retaining the 175,000 PLN total-project planning estimate as unverified.
The consortium sale still requires trust-heavy sponsor and clinic coordination, so fit within the founder's social-energy and time constraints remains unproven.

redesign.economic_effect: Evidence: incumbent wearable-CRO offerings already cover much of the broad stack, Polish device studies can require approvals, sponsor documentation and qualified clinical leadership, and the research found no signed sponsors, clinic capacity, reusable benchmark rights, prices, conversions or renewals. Hypothesis: making two-sponsor deposits, a costed clinic agreement, documented responsibilities and lawful reuse rights hard pre-launch gates transfers first-cohort working-capital risk away from the founder and concentrates reusable learning in one endpoint. Those effects are unvalidated; the consortium may never form, and the unchanged 175,000 PLN total-project figure remains a planning estimate rather than a quote.

risks: The consortium fails to form because sponsors will not share an endpoint, timing or governed benchmark terms.
Participant harm, privacy breach or invalid consent.
Sponsors may prefer established contract research organisations.
EHDS timing and permit rules do not confer near-term or exclusive rights to clinic data.
A study can cross from low-risk benchmarking into a regulated clinical investigation based on intended purpose and protocol design.
Sponsor, clinic, participant and regulatory constraints may prevent the cross-sponsor derived-data rights required for compounding.
The founder cannot personally substitute for required qualified clinical leadership while retaining a full-time job.

structure.control_point: A contract-bound repeat protocol at a named clinic network plus narrowly defined rights to reuse permitted derived metrics across consortium members
structure.critical_dependency: Before launch, enough noncompeting sponsors must precommit funding, qualified clinic roles must accept responsibilities, the regulatory route must be documented, and lawful cross-sponsor derived-benchmark rights must be signed

thesis: Replace the generic validation foundry with a conditional consortium for one fixed EEG or sleep endpoint. The study does not launch unless at least two noncompeting device sponsors fund the governed reference cohort in advance, a named clinic and qualified clinical roles accept costed responsibilities, the protocol-specific regulatory route is documented, and contracts grant only the lawful cross-sponsor derived-benchmark rights required for the shared output. Sponsors receive their own validation analysis plus access to the permitted common benchmark; failure to clear any gate ends the attempt before participant operations or major founder capital is committed.
title: Sponsor-Precommitted EEG/Sleep Reference Consortium
uncertainties: Whether at least two noncompeting EEG or sleep device sponsors will precommit to the same endpoint and fund the cohort before launch
Whether a clinic network and qualified principal investigator will accept costed responsibilities and repeat-protocol terms
Exact regulatory classification by protocol and intended use
Whether contracts, participant information, GDPR and other applicable rules can grant the narrow cross-sponsor derived-benchmark rights the model requires
Recruitment cost, dropout, device loss, clinician-label cost and usable-signal yield
Publicly unobserved sponsor pricing, consortium sales-cycle, conversion, renewal and benchmark-licence demand versus established wearable CROs
Whether sponsor deposits can keep founder cash exposure below available free capital while total project capital remains unquoted
